verdicts.threatModel: The rule models an attacker or workload growing an unbounded Redis keyspace. Ember has no Redis client or server: Cargo.lock and pnpm-lock.yaml contain zero 'redis' entries, so no network cache exists for any attacker to fill.
verdicts.reachability: All 826 member locations (scanner raw file/line in execution.json legacy.data.internal-suite candidates; 526 in crates/raw, 111 crates/engine, 32 crates/tiff, rest in tests/UI) are generic `.set(` calls: TIFF IFD builder tag writes such as `ifd.set(t::COMPRESSION, Value::Short(..))`, JS Map/queue sets in test scripts, and in-memory test fixtures. None reach a Redis sink.
verdicts.impact: None. crates/tiff/src/writer.rs:34-36 shows IfdBuilder::set is `self.entries.insert(tag, value)` into an in-memory map used to build a DNG/TIFF file; there is no retention or expiration semantic to violate and no confidentiality, integrity or availability effect.
verdicts.rationale: Lexical match on `.set(` misclassified as a Redis write; the project has no Redis dependency and sampled sites (crates/engine/src/files.rs:2302, crates/raw/src/dngwrite.rs:140, crates/raw/src/vendor/pef.rs:560, crates/tiff/tests/roundtrip.rs:137, scripts/desktop/slider-command-queue.test.mjs:69) are TIFF tag builders or in-process maps. Devil's advocate: a hidden Redis use via a transitive crate would still appear in Cargo.lock, which has none.

verdicts.threatModel: SQL injection requires attacker-influenced text concatenated into a SQL statement executed by a database engine. Ember links no SQL client (no rusqlite/sqlx/diesel/libsqlite3 in Cargo.lock); its Lightroom import uses an in-repo read-only SQLite file parser (crates/engine/src/lightroom_catalog.rs:11 `lightroom_sqlite::{Database, LiveTable}`) that walks tables, not SQL text.
verdicts.reachability: All 23 members were inspected at their exact lines: 15 are React JSX/template literals building className or label strings (e.g. apps/lightcraft-desktop/web/src/library/Filmstrip.tsx:229, App.tsx:158 `${window.innerWidth}x${window.innerHeight}`), 4 are egui font registration and test asserts containing the words 'select'/'update'/'delete' (crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs:280, crates/pipeline/src/masks.rs:695), 1 a command-registry doc string (crates/engine/src/cmd/denoise.rs:654), and 1 a regex error message (scripts/desktop/gate.mjs:33). No grep hit exists for a SELECT/INSERT INTO/UPDATE/DELETE FROM string literal in crates or apps sources.
verdicts.impact: None. No SQL statement is constructed or executed at any member location, so no query integrity or data confidentiality is at risk.
verdicts.rationale: Scanner keyed on SQL keywords ('select', 'update', 'delete', 'insert') appearing near string interpolation; every site is UI markup, font maps, or test assertion text. Devil's advocate: the Lightroom catalog path does read SQLite, but through a structural parser with no query text and none of the 23 members sit in it.

verdicts.threatModel: The rule models partial database writes across a crash or concurrent writer leaving persisted state inconsistent. No attacker capability is involved; the question is whether adjacent writes target a transactional store.
verdicts.reachability: The 71 members are adjacent `.insert(` calls on in-process HashMap/BTreeMap/serde_json::Map/HashSet values (e.g. crates/desktop-host/src/merge.rs:167 `self.current.insert(..)`, crates/engine/src/lightroom_catalog.rs:662 `geometry.insert("rect"..)`, crates/engine/src/cmd/library.rs:650 `params.insert(k, v)`, apps/lightcraft-cli/src/main.rs:464). The catalog sites (crates/catalog/src/lib.rs:759, keywords.rs:552) mutate in-memory indexes whose persistence goes through the catalog's own append log, not these inserts.
verdicts.impact: None. In-memory map mutations within one function are not durable writes; a crash discards them wholesale, so no torn persisted state or data loss arises from the lack of a transaction boundary at these lines.
verdicts.rationale: Lexical match on multiple `.insert(` calls; none is a database write. Devil's advocate: catalog durability is real, but it is enforced at the log append layer (crates/catalog has dedicated torn-append tests, crates/catalog/src/tests_torn_append.rs), not at these map inserts, so this rule cannot find a defect here.
